In mathematics, a '''Fedosov manifold''' is a [[symplectic manifold]] with a compatible torsion-free [[Connection (mathematics)|connection]], that is, a triple (''M'', ω, ∇), where (''M'', ω) is a [[symplectic manifold]] (that is, <math>\omega</math> is a [[Symplectic manifold|symplectic form]], a non-degenerate closed exterior 2-form, on a <math>C^{\infty}</math>-manifold ''M''), and ∇ is a symplectic torsion-free connection on <math>M.</math><ref name="Fedosov">{{cite arXiv|arxiv=dg-ga/9707024 |last1=Gelfand |first1=Israel |last2=Retakh |first2=Vladimir |last3=Shubin |first3=M. |title=Fedosov Manifolds |date=1997 }}</ref> (A connection ∇ is called '''compatible''' or '''symplectic''' if ''X'' ⋅ ω(''Y,Z'') = ω(∇<sub>''X''</sub>''Y'',''Z'') + ω(''Y'',∇<sub>''X''</sub>''Z'') for all vector fields ''X,Y,Z'' ∈ Γ(T''M''). In other words, the symplectic form is parallel with respect to the connection, i.e., its [[covariant derivative]] vanishes.) Note that every symplectic manifold admits a symplectic torsion-free connection. Cover the manifold with [[Darboux chart]]s and on each chart define a connection ∇ with Christoffel symbol <math>\Gamma^i_{jk}=0</math>.  Then choose a [[partition of unity]] (subordinate to the cover) and glue the local connections together to a global connection which still preserves the symplectic form. The famous result of [[Boris Fedosov|Boris Vasilievich Fedosov]] gives a canonical [[deformation quantization]] of a Fedosov manifold.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Fedosov|first=B. V.|title=A simple geometrical construction of deformation quantization|journal=Journal of Differential Geometry|volume=40|year=1994|issue=2|pages=213–238|doi=10.4310/jdg/1214455536|mr=1293654|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Examples ==

For example, <math>\R^{2n}</math> with the standard symplectic form <math>dx_i \wedge dy_i</math> has the symplectic connection given by the exterior derivative <math>d.</math> Hence, <math>\left(\R^{2n}, \omega, d\right)</math> is a Fedosov manifold.
